I guess if I had to chose my main hobby would be various kinds of creative writing, but mostly in the form of roleplaying with others. Could you explain more on this roleplayong creative writing? It sounds very interesting.

Of course! It varies a lot in format depending on where it happens, people do this sort of thing by email, social networks, journals (livejournal, dreamwidth, etc), blogs, forums (my fave <3) and basically anything you can write on with someone else.

In general an rpg will have a cohesive theme, say, it will be set in the Harry Potter universe, at Hogwarts, and I might play Hermione and someone else will play Harry, another will play Ron and so on and so forth and you make up stories together playing your own character and reacting to what theirs do and say in the same threads you're in.

They may also be more general and an "original" concept (original being pretty relative, most stories share a lot no matter who wrote them or how). Like a horror game where everyone is trapped in a dangerous house or the woods or something, or a real life game. It's not unlike tabletop in some ways, except in almost all circumstances there's no real stats to keep track of or dice to randomise things. Players work out between themselves or themselves and the mod/creator of the game how things are going to go.

Wow, any more info about the "Mesh Network" ?

Sure, here are the people that are writing the software: http://www.broadband-hamnet.org/

Not to be confused with the "dark net", where people are pissed off at the Internet companies. This is all amateur radio, part 97 compliant stuff, emergency communication. Means no encryption over the p2p links and no Internet access since we can't guarantee stuff due to TLS. The FCC doesn't allow us to use encryption over these public bands.

Seems the first half of the 802.11b range falls into amateur radio bands, so we can use higher gain antennas. Technically we can use more power as well, but using commodity hardware this is difficult to do. Part of the 5GHz band falls into this category as well but we're not using that portion... yet.
